newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses hurt by Wall Street's big drop.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses hurt by Wall Street's big drop.

text.p: European bourses started the week with steep losses on Monday, badly rattled by Wall Street's two percent drop on Friday caused by of fears of higher U.S. interest rates.

On currency markets, the dollar was stronger against the mark and yen as traders pondered whether Friday's rout was the start of trend weakness or just a correction. Sterling was also looking more robust.
London, Frankfurt and Paris stocks all tumbled by about one percent at the opening before recovering somewhat. Europe's performance was virtually a rerun of the poor showing on Friday.

London investors were unsettled by New York,which ended 156.78 points off at 8,031.22 on Friday. Things were helped a little by inflation figures on Monday which were at the low end of forecasts but the mood remained edgy.
"The future of the market hangs on whether the interest rate cycle has indeed peaked and we'll have evidence of that all through the week," said a dealer.
"The market's nervous about whether it's peaked and despite the drop on Friday, the FTSE (100) was up about 130 points on the week so thing's look rather vulnerable," said another dealer.

Lonndon's blue-chip FTSE 100 index was down 64.9 points to 4,966.4 at one stage. This was well below the psychologically important 5,000-point barrier it breached last week for the first time, leaving some investors worried that the bull run had gone too far, too fast.

In Frankfurt, stocks opened down about one percent but recovered some ground by mid-morning. "The sell-off this morning was on the back of Wall Street and the dollar, but it has been squeezing back since that. Not exactly a huge correction," a Frankfurt broker said.

"People were keeping an eye on the Bund (government bonds) this morning and the fact that it is positive has helped to stabilise things in the equity market. But generally this is real Monday morning stuff, volumes are thin and you have traders selling off from Friday," he said.

On the downside, shares in pharmaceuticals group Altana AG were the biggest losers. Altana was down 13 marks, or 7.98 percent, at 150 marks. Dealers said there was speculation in the market about problems over further development of its Pantoprazol product, but no-one at Altana was available for comment.
Paris too clawed back some of its early losses but was still down 0.5 percent. "It's relatively calm, it's not a huge sell-off," equity salesman John Fordyce at Oddo said.
Blue chips led the declines, including Alcatel Alsthom, down 1.52 percent, with 69 million francs in trades and Elf-Aquitaine down 1.32 percent.

In currency markets, the dollar was at 1.8557 marks and 115.70 yen, up a pfennig and half a yen on the levels seen on Friday after it plunged four pfennigs and over four yen. But a sustained recovery might be difficult, dealers said.
"Nervousness will continue even though at this stage people are more inclined to be buyers than sellers," said Chris Furness, foreign exchange strategist at 4Cast Ltd in London.

Furness said the market was a directionless, with no U.S. data scheduled for Monday and as traders awaited the Bundesbank's repo announcement on Tuesday. "Nobody is quite prepared to put their foot into the water yet," he said.
The sharp decline of the dollar last week was in part triggered by simmering speculation that the Bundesbank might nudge the repurchase rate higher from 3.00 percent at Tuesday's repo tender.

The sell-off accelerated late in Europe on Friday after Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing was quoted in a newspaper as saying German price developments were moving in the wrong direction in all areas, including consumer prices.

The British pound rebounded three pfennigs to 2.9470 marks and was up four cents to $1.5889 in early trade from Friday's dramatic falls. Sterling has been badly hit by official signals that British interest rates had peaked for the time being.
But chartists said an extension to the recovery faces tough initial resistance at 2.95 marks and $1.59.
"Sterling is the only one of the major crosses which has seen a trend reversal," said Nico Bakker, technical analyst at ABN-Amro in Amsterdam.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.8557 marks and 115.70 yen, compared with 1.8453 and 115.12 in late trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 23.6 points at 5,007.7.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was 27.90 points down at 4,326.25 in bourse floor trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was down 14.60 points at 2,981.05.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $324.85 an ounce in the morning, down from Friday's London close of $325.05. Silver was steady at $4.41.
